observedBehavior.api: any of the twelve module methods after stop
observedBehavior.observed: threw: Exception in HostFunction: E_MODULE_DISPOSED: AccessibilityManager

decisions: AccessibilityManager follows iOS's RCTAccessibilityManager, the contract AccessibilityInfo.js takes when Platform.OS is godot; the Android AccessibilityInfo module is not installed and its lookup returns null.

The module takes the first reading when it is created (as RCTAccessibilityManager does in init), and a getter answers the last reading; the host reads the four settings once per frame, before it drains the queued work, because Godot has no change signal.

A reading is an integer or it is unknown: a missing DisplayServer method or a non-integer answer is -1, never off; a getter rejects E_ACCESSIBILITY_UNKNOWN for -1 and E_ACCESSIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE for the four settings Godot cannot read.

A change is a known value that differs from the last known one: unknown emits nothing, -1 after -1 emits nothing, a return to the last known value emits nothing, and the first known value after only unknown ones is a change.
Everything that names a setting (getter, event, snapshot key, error description, meta key, DisplayServer method) is one row of one table in native/accessibility_info_core.h.

The probe holds the names to the engine's: in headless all four real readings are -1, so it checks that each setting's displayMethod exists in the DisplayServer and that the engine's answer is what the host last read; the oracle holds the four names to its own list.
The probe waits for the poll counter the host reports (frames delivered), never for time, and the oracle checks the host polled at least the frames it waited for and no more after stop.
A focus accessibility event fails out loud and is declared in the report as an engine error the run provokes on purpose; every other type is ignored and counted by type, as iOS does.
Public getters (promises) after stop are not observed: a stopped runtime drains no microtasks. The twelve methods of the retained module and the public announcement carry the E_MODULE_DISPOSED check.

setAccessibilityContentSizeMultipliers validates (E_ARGUMENT for a value that is not null, undefined or a number above zero) and throws E_UNSUPPORTED for a valid argument; iOS stores any number and repairs it to 1.0 on use.
limitations: Local macOS arm64 evidence; hosted CI and Pages are pending and recorded after the merge; other export targets are separate.

The headless engine reports -1 for all four settings, so no real value is read by the suite: values come from the validation meta. A real VoiceOver, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast change is not exercised.

In headless a swap of two DisplayServer methods that both exist would read the same -1 and pass: the suite proves each method exists and is answered as the host read it, and that the names are the oracle's list of Godot 4.7.2's, not that the method is the right one for a machine that reports a value.

Announcements (announceForAccessibility, announceForAccessibilityWithOptions), programmatic focus (setAccessibilityFocus, and sendAccessibilityEvent focus) and announcementFinished wait for GF-20 slice 2b.
Godot's mobile servers report -1 today, so every getter rejects E_ACCESSIBILITY_UNKNOWN there; the iOS and Android bridges are GF-34 and GF-35.
Bold text, grayscale, inverted colors, cross-fade transitions and the content size category have no backing in Godot: they reject, and their events never fire.
A change is seen at the next frame: there is no change callback to wait for.
The screen reader is VoiceOver alone on macOS; Windows and Linux values are unverified.
Text scale (setAccessibilityContentSizeMultipliers, fontScale) and a graphical CI run are out of this slice.
